title: JSON Output Chaos Prompt Lab
summary: Working experiment bank of prompts and stress scenarios designed to surface structured-output formatting edge cases during model onboarding. Focus is on deliberate "chaos" inputs: mixed types, stray punctuation, locale variants, and aggressive truncation to test schema adherence and robustness of post-processing parsers.
background: We're onboarding several community/third-party decoder-only models that have different tendencies around tokenization and punctuation. Past onboarding runs have shown recurring failures: numeric fields returned as strings with commas, arrays collapsed into comma-separated strings, unexpected extra keys, and occasional inclusion of explanatory prose inside JSON. This lab collects targeted prompts to systematically provoke these failure modes so we can measure regressions across model versions and runtime quantization settings.
objective: Create a repeatable prompt-suite that: (1) elicits strictly JSON-only responses across variants, (2) stresses field typing (ints, floats, booleans, null), (3) verifies array vs scalar formatting, (4) tests ordering invariants where clients rely on order, and (5) captures cases that break common JSON parsers (trailing commas, comments, unescaped control chars). The suite should be usable both in hosted evaluation harness and in-local offline runs.
prompt_sets: Invoice-Strict: 'Return EXACTLY one JSON object that matches the schema: {"invoice_id": string, "date": string (YYYY-MM-DD), "total_amount": number (no separators), "items": array of {"sku":string, "qty":integer, "unit_price":number}, "paid": boolean}. Do not include any explanation, newlines allowed only inside the JSON. Example schema only, do not output the word schema.'

Invoice-Noise: 'Same schema as Invoice-Strict but prefix the user instruction with: "Customer comment: Thanks for the speedy delivery! \n Invoice starts below:" and include random emojis and parentheses. Goal: ensure model strips noise and emits clean JSON.'

Number-Locale: 'Produce JSON {"value": <number>} for these inputs: "1,234.56", "1.234,56", "1234,56", "1234.56" and indicate canonical numeric type (no commas) in the output. Expected: numbers as numeric types, not strings.'
Array-vs-String: 'Return {"tags": ...} where tags is an array. Give examples where user input is "tag1, tag2" vs "[tag1, tag2]" vs "tag1;tag2". The model must always output a JSON array of strings.'

Truncate-Test: 'Output JSON object with a nested "notes" string of length exactly 512 characters. If model truncates, mark as failure. Ensure model can produce long token sequences in string fields (escape newlines properly).'

Extra-Keys-Aggro: 'Return JSON for a minimal schema but intentionally attempt to coax model into adding extra explanatory keys (e.g., "confidence", "explanation"). Verify policy: only allow keys in allowed_keys list; if model returns others, annotate as violation.'
Escaping-Control: 'Produce JSON where a field "raw_text" contains various control characters: newlines, tabs, backslashes, quotes, and a unicode emoji. Ensure the JSON is valid and parsable.'

Comment-Comma-Fuzzer: 'Prompt model to output JSON but include examples in the instruction that themselves contain trailing commas and C-style comments. Check whether model mirrors those invalid constructs into the output.'
Ordering-Required: 'Return an array of objects representing steps; preserve the exact order from input. Some clients depend on stable order — test model randomness across 10 seeds.'

Type-Flip: 'Feed the model contradictory examples where the same field is an int in one example and a string in another. Probe how model decides the output type and whether it can be coerced consistently.'
test_matrix: Field-type checks: is_numeric, is_integer, is_boolean, is_null for each field
Schema-strictness: extra_keys_allowed? (true/false) — measure rate of additional keys per 100 responses
Parser-compatibility: run returned JSON through 3 parsers (python json, node JSON.parse, a strict JSON-LD validator) and record failures
Stability over seeds: 10 runs per prompt with different temperature/seed, compute entropy of structure (presence/absence of optional fields)
Localization stress: decimal separators, date formats, thousands separators
Whitespace & escaping: unescaped quotes, literal newlines vs \n, unicode escapes vs raw characters
Large field stress: nested objects depth 5+, large arrays 200+ items, long strings 10k chars
Recovery scenarios: prompt with intentional malformed example to see if model self-corrects
evaluation_criteria: Strict JSON parseability: output must be parseable by standard JSON parsers with no pre-cleaning
Type fidelity: numeric fields must be numeric types, not strings with punctuation
No extraneous prose: responses containing non-JSON prose are failures
Array invariants: fields declared as arrays must not be emitted as delimited strings
Robust escaping: control characters must be properly escaped according to JSON spec
Deterministic ordering (where required): measure order flips across runs and treat >5% flips as regression
notes_to_self: Priority: add automated pre-checks in the hosted API test harness to detect common bad patterns (leading/trailing commas, top-level text before JSON). Add a small set of guided 'repair' heuristics but only as a last-resort; prefer rejecting and surfacing failure to the caller for safety. Also: coordinate with console team to show schema regression diffs in the rollout UI.
